critiques.description: The evidence assessment for control mapping map-060 treats the retention contradiction as undermining the applicability of req-DATA-002, even though the cited evidence supports that the requirement applies; the contradiction instead affects how (or whether) the requirement is satisfied.
critiques.rationale: eas-089 acknowledges that evd-003 and evd-006 together "clearly" and "plausibly" support applying req-DATA-002 to export files as sensitive working data stored in a managed object store, but then concludes that the mapping’s basis "cannot be cleanly validated" and marks map-060 as contradicted. Both evd-003 and evd-006 agree that completed exports are written to managed object storage and subject to some retention behaviour; what they disagree on is the exact retention period (immediate deletion after download vs. 30-day lifecycle). That contradiction is central to assessing how req-DATA-002 is met, but it does not call into question that a retention-focused requirement applies at all. Map-060 already limits itself to `applicable` + `unverified` and explicitly notes in its assumptions that the customer-facing retention story is unclear, while gap-015 separately records the documentation inconsistency. Treating the mapping’s applicability as "contradicted" overstates the impact of the retention disagreement and duplicates what gap-015 is already tracking. It would be more accurate for the assessment to distinguish between applicability (supported by evd-003 and evd-006) and satisfaction (dependent on resolving the contradiction) rather than classifying the mapping itself as contradicted.
